description: Runs managed MongoDB deployments and provides an API for administering Atlas organizations and projects.
access_note: An organization owner creates organization credentials. Project roles govern access to existing projects.
blocker: An Atlas owner must provision scoped credentials. Database queries need a separate connection.
toolkit: Build read-only project and cluster inventory first. Keep database access in a separate tool.
unknowns: Availability and limits for each operation on free clusters.

sources.note: Atlas documents OAuth2 service accounts and HTTP Digest key pairs, owner privileges, and the boundary between the admin API and database contents.
The v2 reference includes an alerts group and separates project and organization resources.
The vendor's MCP tool list includes Atlas projects, clusters, users and performance recommendations.

description: Unifies application logs, metrics, traces and incidents for operations teams.
access_note: Datadog advertises a 14-day trial. Key creation and available telemetry depend on account permissions and configuration.
blocker: No initial trial gate documented. Read operations may require an application key in addition to the API key.
toolkit: Start with scoped incident and metric lookups. Support OAuth for customer installations.
unknowns: Ongoing free-plan coverage by product.

sources.note: The HTTP REST reference specifies the API-key header plus an application-key header for some endpoints.
Datadog documents scoped OAuth bearer tokens and checks the authorizing user's permissions.
The vendor describes its MCP server and offers a 14-day trial of the product suite.
The vendor's MCP repository lists logs, metrics, traces and incidents.
The publisher explicitly identifies this Datadog MCP implementation as independent.

description: Tracks application errors, performance events and releases.
access_note: Users can create personal scoped tokens in settings or an internal integration. A free Developer plan exists. Endpoint-by-endpoint entitlements were not verified.
blocker: Choose user or integration tokens according to the required endpoint. DSN access is limited.
toolkit: Give an agent issue lookup and project triage with narrow scopes.
unknowns: Plan-specific entitlement for advanced operations. Legacy API keys are disabled for new accounts.

sources.note: The auth guide documents personal and integration tokens, OAuth2 for third parties, and DSN auth for certain endpoints.
The versioned web API groups project, organization and event operations and supports region-specific routing.
The issue-list endpoint returns events associated with a specified project.
The help center confirms that Sentry offers a free Developer plan.
The registry entry identifies getsentry as publisher of the Sentry MCP server.
MSPbotsAIFramework publishes its own Sentry API v0 MCP implementation.

description: Organizes pages, structured databases and collaborative workspace content.
access_note: Owners on Free workspaces can create connections. Shared pages and granted capabilities limit the integration's view.
blocker: A connection needs explicit access to the target content.
toolkit: Start with scoped page search and structured database updates.
unknowns: Enterprise admin API and private-beta agent features have separate entitlements.

sources.note: The owner can create a connection on Free. Internal/personal tokens, OAuth connections and page/database event notifications are described.
The create-view reference uses a Bearer header and shows how to attach linked database views to pages.
Notion's reference describes REST-style operations on page and database resources.
Notion's own repository publishes its first-party MCP server and page tools.
A separate publisher implements page, comment, database and file tools against Notion's API.

description: Combines relational bases with spreadsheet-style records and views.
access_note: Free workspaces receive 1,000 API calls per month. Personal tokens and OAuth are supported across plans.
blocker: The free workspace quota and per-base request rate constrain polling.
toolkit: Prototype record lookup and upsert with caching and request backoff.
unknowns: Customer-specific data and base permissions.

sources.note: The Web API guide lists all-plan base creation, personal tokens or OAuth, and the Free monthly allowance.
Airtable documents REST semantics, rate limits, and operations on base records.
Airtable says its hosted MCP runs through the same public REST API and includes the Free plan.
An independently published MCP server exposes Airtable bases to agents.

description: Tracks issues, projects and planning work for software teams.
access_note: Free workspaces receive documented API limits. Admins and permitted members create personal keys, while workspace administration governs OAuth apps.
blocker: Workspace policy can restrict who creates keys.
toolkit: Reuse the issue and project schema for agent search and updates.
unknowns: Customer-specific key policy and rate budget.

sources.note: Linear lists personal keys and OAuth2 against the public GraphQL query/mutation endpoint.
The workspace API settings support webhooks and app creation, and members may create keys when permitted.
The rate-limit table explicitly includes authenticated requests on Free workspaces.
Linear documents its hosted server and supported login methods.
The community server exposes issues and its maintainer points users toward Linear's newer official implementation.

description: Tracks project issues, workflows and permissions in Jira Cloud.
access_note: Atlassian offers free development sites. Scripts can use a user's email and API token; public integrations use OAuth and the user's permissions.
blocker: Privileged project actions still need the corresponding Jira permission.
toolkit: Start with issue search, creation and status updates scoped to one project.
unknowns: Entitlements for particular admin features.

sources.note: The Jira Cloud REST v3 reference publishes issue paths and administrative permissions.
Jira documents OAuth 2.0 (3LO), Basic auth with an account token, and project-admin permission for project updates.
The vendor's developer bundle grants free development sites for Jira products.
Atlassian documents the Rovo MCP server's OAuth flow and exceptions for certain tool sets.
The sooperset implementation targets Jira and Confluence independently of Atlassian Rovo.

description: Coordinates work across tasks, projects and portfolios.
access_note: Asana directs developers to a free account for API testing. A personal token is available in the developer console; dedicated sandboxes have separate eligibility.
blocker: Token permissions and premium project features bound what each user can do.
toolkit: Offer project-task reads and scoped task mutations. Use OAuth for external installations.
unknowns: Service-account and portfolio entitlements vary.

sources.note: The build guide recommends testing the REST API using a free account and personal token before switching to OAuth.
The personal-token guide explains token generation and distinguishes personal, OAuth and service-account tokens.
The FAQ names attachments, projects, tasks and portfolios as API objects.
Asana publishes MCP integration instructions and differentiates MCP access tokens from standard API tokens.
The maintainer describes a local stdio server for Asana REST and distinguishes it from the hosted Asana server.

description: Coordinates team workflows around boards, groups and work items.
access_note: Developers can create a free developer account to generate a personal token and test. App installations can authorize through OAuth.
blocker: Account and board permissions limit the querying user's view.
toolkit: Expose board reads and item updates, asking only for the fields an agent needs.
unknowns: Guest access differs from member access.

sources.note: The authentication guide explicitly ties free developer signup to obtaining an API token for testing.
The support guide identifies GraphQL, personal tokens and an OAuth application authorization flow.
Board queries return columns, groups and paginated items with their attributes.
The hosted monday MCP server runs tools against the same GraphQL API.
The author identifies this as an independent MCP implementation targeting monday.com's GraphQL API.

description: Manages workspaces, lists, work views and tasks.
access_note: Any ClickUp user can generate a personal token. The public API is available on all plans, including Free Forever.
blocker: Some view types have no public endpoint; plan-dependent rate budgets apply.
toolkit: Scope tools to supported task and list resources and use OAuth for shared apps.
unknowns: Coverage differs between v2 and v3.

sources.note: The vendor confirms API availability across plans and personal-token creation for every account, alongside OAuth 2.
The developer guide shows the bearer header for OAuth access tokens.
The reference documents a GET endpoint for tasks under a specific list.
The view guide identifies supported hierarchy and task operations, and excludes some view types.
ClickUp documents its own MCP, including Free Forever and plan-specific limits.
An independent Python server implements task lookups and comments.

description: Combines collaborative documents with interactive tables and automations.
access_note: Coda's vendor-published API collection says the API is free across free and paid workspaces. Doc creation can require a Doc Maker or admin.
blocker: Doc creation can require a higher workspace role; oversized docs may lose API access.
toolkit: Start with row search and upsert in an existing doc.
unknowns: Check size and workspace settings for the target doc.

sources.note: The v1 reference shows bearer-authenticated operations on docs, pages, tables and rows.
Coda's official Postman collection describes free access on both free and paid workspaces and the role needed for doc creation.
The help article documents size-related restrictions on developer API calls.
Coda gives MCP connection instructions and specifies a limited allowance on free plans.
The maintainer identifies this as a community-built Coda server for listing tables and rows.

description: Provides collaborative sheets, rows and project reporting for teams.
access_note: The API is restricted to Business and Enterprise. Eligible users generate an access token from personal settings.
blocker: Business or Enterprise entitlement is required before issuing usable credentials.
toolkit: Offer sheet and row operations to eligible customers and gate setup on plan.
unknowns: Trial API entitlement was not established.

sources.note: The developer introduction explicitly restricts API use to Business and Enterprise plans.
The help center provides self-service access-token generation instructions for eligible users.
The token reference documents OAuth access-token exchange and renewal.
Smartsheet says its generally available MCP routes through its REST API for rows, columns, cell history and comments.
A separate maintainer wraps Smartsheet read endpoints for querying rows from Kiro or another MCP client.

description: Tracks time, expenses, projects and invoices for services teams.
access_note: Developers generate a personal token or register an OAuth application in Harvest ID. Harvest offers free and trial accounts; the API guide does not map each method to a plan.
blocker: Requests require the user's token and Harvest account ID.
toolkit: Start with time-entry lookup and timer actions, then add invoice reads.
unknowns: Confirm plan eligibility for the desired invoice features.

sources.note: Harvest ID issues personal tokens and supports user authorization through OAuth2.
The v2 overview explicitly describes REST, bearer headers, project, time and expense operations, and account-level headers.
Harvest lists a free plan and a trial without separately enumerating per-endpoint API entitlements.
The Harvest MCP guide documents time tracking, invoice limitations and the direct REST fallback for invoice payments.
A separate maintainer publishes an MCP for Harvest time entries using a personal access token.

description: Provides programmable payments, billing and connected-account infrastructure.
access_note: A new account can test in a sandbox before business verification. Live services and marketplace publication require activation.
blocker: For live money movement, account verification and service activation apply.
toolkit: Prototype customer and invoice lookup with restricted sandbox credentials; separate live activation.
unknowns: Production feature availability depends on account and country.

sources.note: Stripe describes its resource-oriented REST API, mode-specific keys and isolated sandboxes.
Stripe documents secret and restricted keys over Basic auth, plus workload identity federation for short-lived credentials.
The Connect OAuth flow covers account authorization and discusses customers, charges and invoices.
A new account can test without configuring payment processing. Live use requires business verification and activation.
Stripe's marketplace identifies its own server for API actions and documentation search.

description: Connects applications to bank-account information and financial products.
access_note: Sandbox access is free. A trial can support limited live work; full Production requires company and use-case approval.
blocker: Full Production requires review. A sandbox credential provides synthetic data.
toolkit: Build against synthetic Items, then seek Production approval for the intended product.
unknowns: Live trial eligibility and allowed institutions vary.

sources.note: The API uses JSON over HTTP POST with a client ID and secret. Linked Item data can require its own access token.
Plaid explicitly offers developer use of Sandbox free of charge.
Production applicants supply company and use-case information. Live trial and Limited Production coverage differ.
The accounts reference describes linked accounts, balances and product-dependent freshness.
Plaid lists distinct Sandbox mock-data tools and a Production Dashboard MCP for operational analytics.

description: Offers exchange market data, account resources and programmatic spot trading.
access_note: Public market data is available without a private account credential. Spot Testnet users receive virtual assets and register their own keys.
blocker: Private methods need signed requests. Testnet omits some production API families.
toolkit: Start with public data or virtual-fund Spot Testnet tools. Assess live permissions separately.
unknowns: Live account and regional eligibility are outside the public-data prototype.

sources.note: Binance separates public market data from signed requests and documents HMAC, RSA and Ed25519 signatures.
The official Spot Testnet guide documents registration, API keys, automatically allocated virtual balances and omitted endpoints.
The official Binance repository distinguishes Spot REST methods and WebSocket market streams.
Binance publishes its own server and explains how users authorize the agent against supported account functions.

description: Paygent Connect is a candidate marketplace-payments and merchant-onboarding product. Its NMI affiliation is unresolved.
access_note: A candidate vendor page markets Paygent Connect and mentions sandbox testing. It does not establish an NMI affiliation or an issuer of Connect-specific credentials.
blocker: Confirm the vendor and its developer documentation before attributing gateway credentials or endpoints.
toolkit: Request the customer's canonical vendor URL or their gateway onboarding documentation.
unknowns: Whether gopaygent.com is the intended NMI-powered product.
Connect-specific auth, price, API and MCP remain unresolved.

sources.note: The candidate marketing page explicitly names Paygent Connect for marketplace payments, revenue sharing and onboarding. Its platform API examples do not establish the NMI relationship.

description: Audits foreign-exchange transactions against benchmark rates and reports spreads.
access_note: Indexed vendor docs describe dashboard API keys. The site distinguishes free individual audits from an API upgrade, and separately advertises a small free MCP allowance.
blocker: The free website estimator, MCP audit allowance and standalone REST entitlement have different descriptions. Confirm the intended route.
toolkit: A narrow FX-audit tool is documented. Verify credential and pricing terms before scheduling an implementation.
unknowns: The live HTML renderer returned generic site copy for indexed deep links. Verify current API tier and quota with the vendor.

sources.note: The indexed vendor API reference documents three REST methods and an API key sent as a bearer token.
The vendor's indexed MCP guide describes a dashboard key, a small free daily allowance and a paid forensic-report tool.
The vendor site presents five free audits and advertises an upgrade for API access. This does not confirm a free standalone REST key.

description: Provides bookkeeping, customer records and financial transactions for businesses.
access_note: Developer sandbox credentials support testing. The independent production credential set requires Intuit questionnaire approval.
blocker: Production keys require Intuit's assessment, and each company authorizes the app.
toolkit: Build read-only bookkeeping workflows in a sandbox while preparing the production questionnaire.
unknowns: Specific GraphQL operations and production pricing vary by product and region.

sources.note: Intuit's QuickBooks Online overview names REST and GraphQL and describes the Accounting API and sandbox development.
The Intuit developer support answer identifies customer, vendor and company objects, OAuth2 and free developer access.
Intuit confirms separate testing and production credentials, with production key questionnaire approval.
Intuit publishes a QuickBooks Online MCP server with OAuth-based access to sandbox or company data.

description: Manages accounting transactions, contacts, invoices and reporting.
access_note: Create a free Xero account, enable the demo company and register an OAuth2 app. The free Starter tier supports up to five connections.
blocker: Moving beyond five connected organizations requires a paid developer tier.
toolkit: Use the demo company for a read-only accounting toolkit. Model connection-based pricing before a wide rollout.
unknowns: Commercial tier and feature eligibility for the intended deployment.

sources.note: The developer guide walks through free signup, demo company setup and registering an OAuth2 app.
The OAuth documentation specifies the authorization code/PKCE options and five-connection Starter cap.
The accounting reference shows invoice resources with GET and POST/PUT operations and related contact records.
The vendor FAQ describes invoices, contacts, bank transactions, tier caps and Xero's official developer MCP option.

description: Provides corporate cards, spend management and financial operations for businesses.
access_note: An existing account or card admin can generate an internal user token. Partner OAuth credentials and a staging account require Brex involvement.
blocker: A distributed app must obtain partner credentials and complete Brex onboarding.
toolkit: Prove expense or transaction reads with a customer admin, then request partner OAuth and staging.
unknowns: Partner contract and sandbox turnaround.

sources.note: Brex documents REST/OpenAPI and lists cards, expenses, reimbursements and payments.
A Brex account or card admin can create a scoped user token in the dashboard.
Brex issues a client ID and secret on request for the partner OAuth client-credentials route.
Partner onboarding covers an access agreement and manually provisioned staging accounts.
Brex describes its own MCP and requires Developer API access and admin enablement.

description: Manages corporate cards, transactions, reimbursements and spend controls.
access_note: A form provisions a demo sandbox. Admins can create apps for their own Ramp business; distributing to other businesses requires two approvals.
blocker: Multi-tenant production requires both partner approval and app-specific production approval.
toolkit: Use a sandbox to build spend reads and pursue the two approvals in parallel with design.
unknowns: Unpublished scope entitlements for individual businesses.

sources.note: Ramp distinguishes sandbox signup, internal admin credentials and two approval steps for external production apps.
The authorization guide documents OAuth2 client credentials and delegated access with scoped tokens.
The REST reference documents card-transaction collection and individual-resource paths.
Ramp's MCP guide records client setup, administrator restrictions and redirect allowlisting.

description: Licenses company, deal, investor and fund data for private-market research.
access_note: PitchBook's Direct Data team evaluates the required datasets and helps establish an API connection.
blocker: The API and licensed datasets come through Direct Data sales; no self-issued key path was established.
toolkit: Seek a licensed pilot focused on company or deal enrichment before building a public toolkit.
unknowns: Exact token format, commercial terms and any API-specific trial.

sources.note: PitchBook states its team helps clients connect through an API key or authentication token. No token transport is specified.
The vendor describes a JSON REST API covering deals, funds, investors and other entity types, with a Direct Data request route.
PitchBook's launch release distinguishes its Data MCP dataset subset from its wider data offerings.

description: Builds source-grounded notebooks for research; the documented API is Gemini Notebook Enterprise.
access_note: A licensed user, Google Cloud project and IAM role are required. Google documents a 14-day enterprise trial and separate paid subscriptions.
blocker: The documented route requires an enterprise subscription or trial, user licensing and Cloud IAM provisioning.
toolkit: Target enterprise notebook administration. Confirm licenses and region before proposing an integration.
unknowns: No verified equivalent public consumer API or vendor-maintained MCP for the named NotebookLM surface.

sources.note: The REST examples pass a signed-in user's Google access token and require an active enterprise license; they document create, get, list, share and delete.
Google identifies the product rename and specifies the trial, regional licensing and IAM setup.
The RPC reference documents the Google cloud-platform OAuth scope and notebook and source resource names.
An independent publisher offers a NotebookLM MCP implementation, separate from Google's enterprise API.

description: Transcribes meetings and makes conversation content and summaries searchable.
access_note: Otter's standalone public API is available to Enterprise workspaces. Its pricing also lists MCP for Basic users, through a separate OAuth connection.
blocker: Direct API credentials require Enterprise. A user's existing MCP connection has a different entitlement and auth flow.
toolkit: Offer native-MCP setup for supported users. Reserve custom REST automation for Enterprise workspaces.
unknowns: Enterprise trial/API eligibility and customer-specific admin controls.

sources.note: Otter documents Enterprise access, per-user bearer API keys, conversation and channel resources, and workspace analytics.
Otter's pricing distinguishes the Basic MCP feature from Enterprise API and webhooks.
Otter's server guide uses OAuth for the MCP connection. This is distinct from the standalone API key.

description: Records meetings and returns transcripts, summaries and action items.
access_note: Developer API and webhooks are offered on every plan. Individual users issue keys; external integrations use OAuth and can be reviewed.
blocker: Tokens only see owned or shared meetings, and OAuth apps use a dedicated transcript endpoint.
toolkit: Start with user-authorized meeting summaries or transcripts; support the OAuth endpoint differences.
unknowns: Marketplace review and permissions for target customer teams.

sources.note: Fathom lists meeting summaries, action items, transcripts and webhooks on every plan.
A user generates an X-Api-Key and lists meetings. OAuth apps must request transcripts separately instead of expanding the meeting response.
The partner guide registers an OAuth application and explains the review for public integrations.
Fathom's own help center explains connecting its meeting MCP to external AI assistants.
High-Impact-Athletes publishes a separate OAuth-based MCP integration for Fathom meetings.

description: Searches peer-reviewed research and returns citations and study metadata.
access_note: The account dashboard issues an API key. Free accounts get 30 combined API and MCP calls per month; larger quotas and full-text excerpts require paid tiers.
blocker: Direct REST uses x-api-key. OAuth is documented for supported MCP clients; a general REST OAuth flow was not verified.
toolkit: Start with bounded paper-search calls and cite returned studies. Budget shared API/MCP usage.
unknowns: Whether Consensus would offer direct REST OAuth for a multi-user integration.

sources.note: The help center documents dashboard key creation, x-api-key, research filters, threads and the Free cap of 30 shared calls.
Consensus's own repository explicitly labels the search service REST and lists citation and study metadata.
The official MCP guide documents interactive OAuth and API-key configurations for different clients.

description: Converts document files into structured content, extracted fields and classifications.
access_note: Create an account and key in Reducto Studio. The Standard plan starts with a promotional allowance, followed by usage pricing.
blocker: The initial credit allowance is finite; sustained processing is metered.
toolkit: Build a document parse/extract skill and return structured results with source coordinates.
unknowns: Individual signup eligibility and post-credit billing behavior were not tested.

sources.note: The vendor identifies five document-processing endpoints, an OpenAPI reference, Studio key issuance, clients and a CLI.
The quickstart sends the Studio API key as a bearer token in a POST to the parse endpoint.
The Standard pricing table includes promotional API usage before standard rates apply.
Reducto documents a first-party MCP server that can run the document-processing tools.

description: Runs cloud coding sessions and manages reusable engineering playbooks and knowledge.
access_note: The pricing matrix excludes the Devin API on Free and includes it on Pro and higher. Users provision a service identity or use a permitted personal access token.
blocker: An eligible paid plan and a token with organization permissions are required.
toolkit: Use a narrowly scoped service user to retrieve session status and playbooks, then add explicit session creation.
unknowns: Legacy-key instructions differ across docs; use v3 credentials and check the exact MCP tool's auth requirements.

sources.note: The v3 API accepts bearer credentials for a service identity or person. It documents session, knowledge, playbook and enterprise resources.
The vendor comparison matrix uses a cross/dash for the Free column and check marks from Pro onward on the Devin API row.
The dedicated MCP guide documents repository, session and playbook tools and details differences among personal, service-user and legacy credentials.

description: Generates images and video across a catalog of media models.
access_note: A developer generates a key in Open Higgsfield. Direct API generations draw on a separate prepaid balance with a documented minimum top-up.
blocker: API calls consume prepaid money; website plan credits apply to MCP/CLI instead.
toolkit: Offer a cost estimate before generation and keep API balance separate from MCP/CLI plan credits.
unknowns: Promotional access for a specific developer was not established.

sources.note: Higgsfield explicitly documents direct REST, a console key, a separate prepaid balance, a minimum top-up and a request-estimate endpoint.
The quickstart demonstrates obtaining a signed upload URL and using SDKs or direct calls.
The official MCP connects a subscriber's account and spends plan credits. Its entitlement is separate from the developer API.
Higgsfield documents the CLI's browser sign-in and distinguishes it from the API-key route.

description: Renders Mermaid diagram definitions to SVG, PNG or PDF on a local machine.
access_note: Install the public npm package or container and run the CLI locally. This path requires no vendor credential.
blocker: A toolkit must run and provision the local renderer; the documented Node API lacks a semantic-versioning guarantee.
toolkit: Wrap one pinned mmdc render operation in a local skill and return the generated file.
unknowns: A commercial Mermaid Chart MCP also exists; a first-party server for this exact CLI package was not established.

sources.note: The project documents local npm/container installation, rendering diagram input and processing Markdown with the mmdc binary.
The README separately exposes a local Node.js API and warns its interface is outside semantic versioning.
The community server explicitly invokes the named mmdc binary locally.
Mermaid Chart documents an MCP for its diagram service and cloud account. That distinct product is excluded from the CLI-specific official-MCP count.

description: Fetches captions and video or channel metadata through the independent TranscriptAPI.com service.
access_note: Signup includes 100 free credits and a dashboard API key without a card. Some zero-cost endpoints still require a positive credit balance.
blocker: Availability depends on whether usable captions and the video are accessible.
toolkit: Expose transcript lookup and surface explicit no-caption and unavailable-video states.
unknowns: An independent service operates this API; results can depend on upstream video availability.

sources.note: The reference documents bearer API keys, transcript and metadata endpoints, credit requirements and distinct unavailable-caption errors.
The cURL guide specifies 100 signup credits, no card and dashboard-issued keys.
TranscriptAPI's own MCP uses the service's REST extraction, credential and credit infrastructure.
The operator explicitly disclaims affiliation with YouTube or Google.

description: Makes recorded meetings, transcripts, notes and action items accessible to teams.
access_note: Every plan supports personal tokens, including Free. Workspace-wide tokens need Business or Enterprise and a workspace admin. Distributed apps use OAuth2.
blocker: The free token inherits the user's meeting permissions. Workspace-wide export has a separate entitlement.
toolkit: Prototype individual meeting retrieval with a PAT and require OAuth for installations by other users.
unknowns: No separate sandbox; test using an explicitly authorized recording.

sources.note: Grain distinguishes personal, workspace and OAuth2 credentials, lists meeting and webhook capabilities, and says API v1 was sunset.
The v2 developer overview shows a versioned HTTP GET with a PAT transported in a bearer header.
The vendor lists tools available on all plans and additional Business/Enterprise functionality.
The independent publisher provides an MCP server targeting Grain meetings; compatibility with current v2 was not tested.
